content_sections.heading: About the Institute and the Project
content_sections.text: Raman Research Institute is based in Bengaluru, where shortlisted candidates are interviewed. QuIC leads QuEPRAN, the National Quantum Mission technology group building a multi-node quantum repeater network for entanglement-based quantum communication. Its partners are HRI Prayagraj, IIT Tirupati, IIT Patna and IISER Mohali, and Professor Urbasi Sinha is the Lead Principal Investigator. The fellowships lead into the RRI PhD programme through the Alternative Entry to PhD programme (AEP), which admits exceptional students funded through extra-mural grants. According to the notice, entry does not depend on a rank cut-off but on steady work and demonstrated progress in the laboratory.

content_sections.heading: Who Can Apply
content_sections.text: 75% or more marks in aggregate, or equivalent CGPA, in the qualifying degree. Coursework in quantum mechanics and optics. Hands-on experience in an optics laboratory. Programming for data analysis or instrument control (Python, MATLAB or LabVIEW). Those already working in Government, Semi-Government, PSU or Autonomous Bodies shall submit their applications through proper channel. The notice also says the Institute reserves the right to relax any requirement in exceptional cases.

content_sections.heading: Pay and Tenure
content_sections.text: Fellowship: Rs. 37,000 per month plus HRA at the applicable rate (currently 30%) for the first two years. From the third year, for those inducted into the PhD programme: Rs. 42,000 per month plus HRA. Tenure: one year in the first instance. On induction into the PhD programme, the fellowship continues subject to satisfactory progress in six-monthly reviews. If a fellow is not inducted within twelve months of joining, the fellowship ends on completion of one year. This is a project-based position, and remuneration depends on availability of project funding.

content_sections.heading: RRI PhD-track Junior Research Fellowships (JRF) Job Description
content_sections.text: The fellow joins QuIC on the National Quantum Mission project and works on a defined experiment from the first week. The notice lists these thesis-scale problems at the first repeater node: Optical and spin properties of colour centres in diamond, including nitrogen-vacancy, silicon-vacancy and other vacancy centres. Entangled-photon sources compatible with solid-state quantum memories. Light–matter interfaces between single photons and solid-state quantum memories. Bell-state measurement and entanglement swapping between network links. Photonic links in fibre and free space between network nodes. Progress is reviewed at six months. By then the fellow is expected to have: characterised the optical components and sources in the set-up, with quantified uncertainties; read the documentation of the instruments used, and applied it; identified and explained any discrepancy between expected and measured behaviour; built and run an interference experiment from start to finish; presented the work at a group meeting. Between six and twelve months after joining, the Principal Investigator, as prospective supervisor, recommends the fellow for admission through the AEP, and the fellow is interviewed for the RRI PhD programme. A successful interview admits the fellow to the RRI PhD programme, with the same research and the same supervisor, and the fellowship continues from the project grant. Details of the AEP are on the RRI PhD programme page .

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for RRI PhD-track Junior Research Fellowships (JRF)
content_sections.text: Prepare a single PDF containing all the items listed below. Email the PDF to [email protected] . Write the subject line as "PhD-track JRF Application". Make sure the application is received by 31 December 2026; applications received after the closing date will not be considered. A CV with marks or grades from Class 10 onwards. The scorecard or certificate showing the JEST, CSIR-UGC NET or GATE qualification, with the year. A one-page statement on why you want a PhD, why experimental physics, and one experiment you carried out with your own hands, including what went wrong and what you did about it. A short statement showing how you meet the essential and desirable criteria. Names and email addresses of two academic referees. Letters will be requested only from the referees of shortlisted candidates.

content_sections.heading: Selection and Interview
content_sections.text: Selection runs in three steps, as the notice describes them. Applications are shortlisted against the essential and desirable criteria. Letters of recommendation are requested from the referees of shortlisted candidates. A final list of candidates is called for an interview in person at RRI, Bengaluru. The interview covers the fundamentals of quantum mechanics and optics, an experiment the candidate has carried out with their own hands, and their reasons for pursuing an experimental PhD. The Institute may restrict the number of candidates called for interview, on the basis of qualification and experience higher than the minimum prescribed. Meeting the essential and desirable criteria does not entitle an applicant to be called. Second class train fare for attending the interview is reimbursed on production of the original tickets. The notice does not give an interview date.

content_sections.heading: Important Instructions
content_sections.text: The Institute reserves the right not to fill the positions advertised. Canvassing in any form shall disqualify the candidate. Applications received after the closing date will not be considered. The JEST, CSIR-UGC NET or GATE qualification must be valid on the closing date.

faq.question: Q1. How many PhD-track JRF posts has RRI announced?
faq.answer: RRI has announced two PhD-track Junior Research Fellowships in the QuIC laboratory of the Light and Matter Physics group.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply for the RRI JRF posts?
faq.answer: The closing date for receiving applications is 31 December 2026. Applications received after that date will not be considered.

faq.question: Q3. What qualification is needed for the RRI PhD-track JRF?
faq.answer: A Master's degree in Physics, Engineering Physics, Optics or Photonics with at least 55% marks in aggregate or equivalent grade, and qualification in JEST (Physics), CSIR-UGC NET (Physical Sciences) or GATE (Physics). Final semester students may apply.

faq.question: Q4. What is the age limit for the RRI JRF?
faq.answer: The age must be not more than 28 years on the closing date. Relaxation applies as per Government of India rules for SC/ST/OBC candidates and persons with disabilities.

faq.question: Q5. What is the salary of the RRI JRF?
faq.answer: The fellowship is Rs. 37,000 per month plus HRA at the applicable rate (currently 30%) for the first two years. It becomes Rs. 42,000 per month plus HRA from the third year for those inducted into the PhD programme.

faq.question: Q6. How do I apply for the RRI JRF?
faq.answer: Email a single PDF to [email protected] with the subject line "PhD-track JRF Application". The PDF must hold the CV, the national test scorecard, a one-page statement, a criteria statement and two referees' details.

faq.question: Q7. How are candidates selected for the RRI JRF?
faq.answer: Applications are shortlisted against the essential and desirable criteria. Referees of shortlisted candidates are asked for letters, and a final list is called for an in-person interview at RRI, Bengaluru.

faq.question: Q8. Is a JEST, NET or GATE score cut-off required?
faq.answer: No. The notice says qualification is sufficient and no minimum score or rank is required, but the qualification must be valid on the closing date.

faq.question: Q9. Is the RRI JRF a permanent job?
faq.answer: No, it is a project-based position. The tenure is one year in the first instance, and remuneration depends on availability of project funding.

faq.question: Q10. Is HRA paid on top of the fellowship amount?
faq.answer: Yes. The fellowship is Rs. 37,000 per month plus HRA at the applicable rate, currently 30%, and Rs. 42,000 per month plus HRA from the third year for those inducted into the PhD programme.
